author: kevaundray
content:
I saw that 7645 was PFId also in H*, has there been any thought around whether we want it with 8141?

Heres my understanding:

For sender frames/legacy txs, it seems that 8141 and 7645 take different stances:

- 8141 tries to be maximally compatibly with legacy transactions, so origin is the initial caller and does not change within nested calls, while caller is the immediate frame initiator
- 7645 as you know, makes origin == caller, so origin always returns the immediate caller of the evm call frame

If we were to want 7645, then 8141's semantics would likely change I believe, but as you know, this would be a breaking change for existing contracts that rely on this distinction between origin and caller to check if the caller is an EOA. I haven't checked to see what the blast radius of this is

author: kevaundray
content: I guess (as noted) default frames are already not backwards compatible in a similar sense, but less breaking; ie contracts that follow the usual EOA interpretation of origin may not work similarly since origin == caller == entrypoint at the top level call

author: gaxanh
content: This issue has been discussed since before the launch of EIP-7702, and we can now see its immediate impact. At the time, EIP-7645 was merely a step toward formally addressing existing technical debt within the protocol; the anticipated EVM-level effects are expected to automate all transaction types, not just frames.
